bridge_line: Our best known teacher and hymn writer, at Nisibis and later Edessa.

dates.note: In-build attestation (T3-E): syrgrav001 spans "Ephrem's whole corpus (350s-373)". These bound the surviving corpus, not his life; no birth date is attested in this build.

bridge_line: A Persian teacher. His twenty-three written demonstrations survive; no story of his days does.

dates.note: In-build attestation (T3-E), transcribed not supplied: syrgrav001 dates "Aphrahat's earlier Demonstrations (336/7-345)" and syrforce1B2 fixes Demonstration 6 at 337. These bound his known WRITING, not his life - no birth or death date is attested anywhere in this build, and this record's own bridge_line says no story of his days survives.

names: Jacob (Mar Yaqub) of Nisibis, bishop from c. 309
bridge_line: Bishop of Nisibis from about 309. Our sources disagree on when he died.

dates.note: No end_year, deliberately: his death date is a genuine primary-source conflict this record carries open (see attribution_note). Recording either candidate here would settle in a data field what the record refuses to settle in prose.

names: Simeon bar Sabba'e, bishop of Seleucia-Ctesiphon
bridge_line: A bishop in the Persian empire, put to death when the king turned on us.

dates.display: martyred 341 by the traditional date, disputed (Kosinski/Burgess argue c. 344)
dates.note: Transcribed from this record's own attribution_note (T3-E), not supplied from outside it. The dispute is live and load-bearing - the downstream succession chain shifts with it (Doc_02 SS11) - so `display` carries both positions and neither is settled here. end_year holds the traditional date purely as a machine-comparable bound; `approximate` is omitted rather than guessed, because one candidate is a transmitted date and the other a scholarly estimate, and no single flag is true of both.

bridge_line: The teacher our founding account says was sent to Edessa. That account is a later legend.

names: Abgar V (the correspondence legend; Doc_01 SS2's own identification)
bridge_line: The king of Edessa who, our founding account says, wrote to Jesus.
A bishop from outside our tradition. He appears only inside a later legend about Ephrem.
